## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]
- **A57** On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook. [hw]
- **A58** A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording. [hw]
- **A59** Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays. [hw]
- **A60** Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent. [hw]
- **A61** Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2). [doc]
- **A62** When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments. [hw]
- **A63** When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it. [hw]
- **A64** When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads. [hw]
- **A65** Judge a load budget by the playing load and include the new module's own cost. [hw]

- [hw] CPU: ColdFire MCF54415CMJ250 (chip marking read 2026-09-30): MCF5441x, V4 core with EMAC, 250 MHz, no separate DSP. All audio is ColdFire assembly. It is the same CPU family as Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1, Rytm and A4; the Octatrack is the exception. The MCF54418 reference manual applies. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#454f0b95` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:9](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L9) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
- [hw] Audio: 6 tracks, rendered per 32-sample block (0.67 ms) in the audio interrupt. The stock OS already takes about 77 % of each block, even when stopped, because all tracks and effects are computed every block. Peaks reach 99 % with heavy added engines. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#f6da9f46` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:10](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L10) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform

- [doc] [hw] Free space is scarce. The project's main source of code room is freed sprite masks: Groups of byte-identical `0xFF` bitmap masks are each referenced by one 32-bit constant. Redirecting that constant to a kept copy renders identically and frees the others. 10 groups, 164 freeable masks, 104-1,024 bytes each. Never write into a kept copy. - [hw] Mistake 1: reacting to one heavy block. Peaks are isolated: a step where several tracks start (the sequencer takes up to ~7 % of a block), or caches the UI flushed between blocks (+4.6 points). By the time the governor sees such a block, it is already over; cutting a voice can't rescue it and is audible. The fix reacts only to a peak that lasts two blocks, or to sustained load. - [doc] [hw] Knob writes and preview notes: the parameter write `0x40059534(value, track, k)` writes straight into the voice's targets `0x800015ae + 66t + 2k`, so a turned knob reaches a note that already plays. - [emu] USB multitrack glitches (reported on Reddit after 15-20 minutes): Cause: the OS sends each block to USB right after rendering it, and the 6-channel mod's queue tolerated only 0.2 ms of jitter. With variable engine load (muted tracks, effects off) frames went missing. Fix: send at a fixed time at the start of the next interrupt, align the queue at start-up, and use a 9-slot ring instead of 8. Zero defects in the simulator afterwards. General rule for USB streaming mods: decouple the send time from a variable render time. `[emu]` (cause read in the OS, fix simulated) — `model-cycles-samples#e0c972d2` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:55](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L55) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
- [emu] Mistake 2: an integer moving average that never moves. `slow += (load - slow) >> 8` with load and average in whole percent rounds every step to 0, or to -1 below the average. The "sustained load" rule therefore never fired on a unit. The emulator test hid it because it pre-set the average. Keep fixed-point averages in scaled units (e.g. load << 8), and test them from a cold start. `[emu]` — `model-cycles-samples#a5c5bf10` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:72](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L72) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
- [emu] EMAC wrappers are not free: wrapping the reverb kernels in helpers that saved ACC3 and MACSR around every product cost +20-48 % instructions. - [doc] [emu] CC lookup (Model:Cycles): the CC-to-descriptor table is built at `0x4005a8ce`; CC 16-23 are looked up only in the row of the track's machine, so a shared descriptor on CC 20-23 is never reached, while CC 75-78 reach shared descriptors on all six tracks (`[emu]`, interpreter). CC values are not scaled: the handler `0x4000b568` writes value x 256 and the setter `0x4000b274` clamps to the descriptor's range. Edits send their CC through `0x4000b942`, which reads the stock table at `0x4010dce0`. `[doc]` — `model-cycles-samples#81cf7c6a` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:85](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L85) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)

- [doc] Container: ELE3, text header plus section table (16-byte aligned), with a trailer of zero padding, 4 zero bytes and an HMAC-SHA256 at a 16-byte-aligned offset. The key is re-derived from the image itself, so checksums and HMAC can be recomputed. `[doc]` — `model-cycles-samples#acbe3405` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:12](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L12) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
- [doc] Large code is appended to the image and copied to SDRAM at boot by one shared boot hook (Syntakt engines and MACRO at `0x43000000`, Model-TG at `0x46700000`). - [doc] Mistake 3: stealing the quietest voice before the mixer. That ignores track volume, sends and mute, so a naturally quiet but loud-mixed track (hi-hat, a long tail) always went first, and a muted but still computed track was never preferred. - [doc] Voice internals (Model:Cycles): amp envelope `0x400a9252`, decay table `0x4011d84c` (DECAY 127 is about 15 s to -60 dB); the VCA `0x400a9430` clears the level in a trig's block, which clicks on a retrig; PUNCH `0x400a967a` (with PUNCH off a TONE track's output is x1/8); the voice loop `0x400a7d4a` keeps trig and release flags for one block only, runs the EMAC with MACSR `0xa0` and leaves acc0 uncleared; per-track velocity gain at `0x40fe4c90 + 2*track`. `[doc]` — `model-cycles-samples#2ac04fac` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:89](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L89) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)

- [doc] Pads and TRIG keys: the pads play and end notes through `0x4001d05e(view, track, note, velocity, speed)` and `0x4001d0fc(view, track, note)`, called only by the pads' handler `0x4001d180`; the TRIG keys in keyboard mode use `0x40019e7a` (on) and `0x40019c84` (off). Each of the note-on routines begins with `lea -16(sp),sp ; moveq #5,dN`, a clean 6-byte hook site. `[doc]` — `model-cycles-samples#4d691351` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:99](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L99) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Pads, preview notes and the shared sine (model27 notes 60 and 66, MAIN OS 1.13, 2026-11-12)
- [doc] Note ranks: the audio side's event loop keeps, per track, the rank and note that hold it (`0x40fe4c9c + 4t`, `0x40fe4cb4 + 4t`); sequencer notes are rank 1, notes played live rank 2, a note of lower rank is dropped, and a note-off frees the track only with the same rank and note. That is why a held pad or TRIG key pauses the track's own trigs on every stock machine. `[doc]` — `model-cycles-samples#0239456f` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:100](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L100) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Pads, preview notes and the shared sine (model27 notes 60 and 66, MAIN OS 1.13, 2026-11-12)
- [doc] The OS sine `0x8000eee4` (257 Q31 samples in SRAM, copied from the image at boot) is the default wave of every voice operator: the voice reset `0x400a7ab8` (at boot and at each machine change) points all four operators' wave pointers (voice + 168 + 120j) at it. Only KICK (`0x8000eae0` on one operator), METAL (`0x8000f2e8` on two), PERC (`0x4012024c`, in DDR, on one) and CHORD (its own frames) set other waves; SNARE and TONE play only the sine. The waves `0x8000eae0`, the sine and `0x8000f2e8` sit back to back, 1,028 bytes each, after CHORD's last SRAM frame. A mod that rewrites the sine changes every machine. `[doc]` — `model-cycles-samples#e6e5f20e` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:103](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L103) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Pads, preview notes and the shared sine (model27 notes 60 and 66, MAIN OS 1.13, 2026-11-12)
